question.problem: Find the disjoint union of the sets ${A}_{1}=\{3,6\}$ and ${A}_{2}=\{4,6\}.$
question.worked_solution:
Notice that the sets are overlapping since

$$
\{3,6\}\cap \{4,6\}=\{6\}\ne ∅.
$$

So, for each of our sets, we form the associated set, where each element is tagged with the corresponding index, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned} & {A}_{1} &  & \,\to \, &  & {A}_{1}^{∗}=\{(3,1),(6,1)\} \\  & {A}_{2} &  & \,\to \, &  & {A}_{2}^{∗}=\{(4,2),(6,2)\}\end{aligned}
$$

Now, the disjoint union of our sets is simply the union of the associated tagged sets:

$$
\begin{aligned}{A}_{1}⊔{A}_{2} & =\{3,6\}⊔\{4,6\} \\  & ={A}_{1}^{∗}\cup {A}_{2}^{∗} \\  & =\{(3,1),(6,1)\}\cup \{(4,2),(6,2)\} \\  & =\{(3,1),(6,1),(4,2),(6,2)\}\end{aligned}
$$
